title: The antediluvian civilization
statement: The span between the creation and the Flood — the Age of Leo through the Age of Cancer on the corpus's compressed chronology, c. 11,375-6,690 BCE — held a developing human civilization in contact with the exiled creator faction, whose technological development and hybrid lineages are what the Flood decision of woh-claim-0010 was taken against; the biblical genealogies and parallel traditions preserve this span as the antediluvian age.

includes: The span and its dating against the precessional chronology (woh-claim-0003), on the corpus's compressed timeline
The canonical content: a human population in contact with the exiled faction, the unions and their offspring (woh-claim-0012), and the development the Council judged dangerous

The memory layer: the Genesis 5 genealogies, the long lifespans read as the canon reads them, and the parallel antediluvian traditions (the Sumerian king list's antediluvian section above all) as transformed memory of the span
excludes: Archaeological claims about lost antediluvian material culture; the corpus asserts memory in texts, not strata
The literal arithmetic of the genealogies as chronology; the corpus's dating comes from woh-claim-0003, not from summing lifespans
One-to-one identification of named patriarchs with named traditions' antediluvian kings
The Flood decision itself, carried by woh-claim-0010

source_references.locator: Chapter 2 (the antediluvian narrative: the population, the exiled faction's involvement, the development preceding the Flood)
GEN-WOH-5 (the antediluvian genealogies); 6:1-4 (the unions, carried by woh-claim-0012)
The pre-flood narrative frame: the growing population and the disturbance that precedes the decision

alternatives.statement: The Genesis 5 genealogies are schematic theology (declining lifespans as declining nearness to creation); they preserve structure, not a span.
The Sumerian antediluvian king list and Genesis 5 share a literary convention of deep pre-flood time; the convention explains the parallel without a remembered civilization.
No archaeological horizon corresponds to a technological civilization in the claimed span; absence at this scale is evidence of absence.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0001, woh-claim-0003, or woh-claim-0008 is revised or retired.
The Model-C age-lattice reconciliation underlying the corpus's dating is revised.
Public prose begins asserting archaeological claims or genealogical arithmetic, which this record excludes.
Source-language review changes the Genesis 5 observations.
